summary: Attacked the Model theory area, whose single roadmap is LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory (Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration), seven layers LD.0 to LD.6. Two findings, both medium: three layers declare a prerequisite on FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration that is in no `requires` field and in no atlas record, though the roadmap's document exists and 23 roadmaps cite it 41 times; and LD.0 instructs a worker to construct ultraproducts and prove Los's theorem, both of which Mathlib has at the pin. The rest held: every other stage id resolves, the roadmap's prerequisites and consumer exist, the four Part II proposals routed here all carry titles that obey section 15, nothing in the area is planned twice elsewhere in the atlas, and every other target the layers plan is genuinely absent from both libraries.
checked: All seven layers of the roadmap, its document and its stage records, and the sixteen paper routes that reach the area (twelve as a source, four proposing Part II roadmaps).

Prerequisite structure, which produced finding 1: every stage-level `requires` entry resolves to a real stage, the roadmap's four prerequisites (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion, DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles, SchemeAndStackFoundations) and its consumer AnalyticNumberTheory all exist, and 13 stage edges are recorded. The failure is not in `requires` but between `requires` and the prose: three layers name inputs that the field omits and the atlas cannot resolve.
Each layer's prose Inputs against its `requires` field, one by one. LD.3, LD.4, LD.5 and LD.6 match exactly; LD.0, LD.1 and LD.2 do not, and all three mismatches are the same missing roadmap.

The pinned libraries against every notion the seven layers plan, with the searches run correctly rather than by a pattern that silently matches nothing. Absent at the pin, and so rightly planned: o-minimal structures and cell decomposition, Ax-Kochen-Ershov and Denef-Pas, motivic integration, Pila-Wilkie and Pila-Zannier, Andre-Oort and Zilber-Pink, MRDP and Hilbert's tenth problem, angular components. Present, and so wrongly planned: ultraproducts and Los's theorem, which is finding 2. Partly present and correctly described as something to develop: henselianity, where Tau Ceti has HenselianRing and henselianLocalRing_integer but not the elimination results LD.1 wants.

The four Part II proposals routed off this roadmap, against section 15's title rule. All four are exact prefix extensions of the parent's atlas title 'Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration': HilbertTenthProblemOverRingsOfIntegers from PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26, EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations from PAPER-BINYAMINI-22, FinitelyGeneratedFieldDefinability from PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 and LogicAndDefinabilityPartII from PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19. Four Part IIs for one parent is not itself duplication: they run in four different directions.

Duplication against the whole atlas, for the eight concepts this area could plausibly share: o-minimality and cell decomposition, Pila-Wilkie, Andre-Oort and Zilber-Pink, motivic integration, Ax-Kochen-Ershov and Denef-Pas, Hilbert's tenth problem, ultraproducts, and functional transcendence. Four of the eight occur in no other roadmap at all. The four that do were read and none duplicates this area: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.5 says it coordinates 'unlikely intersections with RP' rather than owning them; ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6 is dynamical Mordell-Lang in its own setting; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.4 fixes a nonprincipal ultrafilter to run Taylor-Wiles ultrapatching, consuming ultraproducts rather than building them; and the IgusaVarieties and GeometricTopology hits are false positives of the search.

Whether any restructuring proposal already resolves either finding. Two do name the roadmap, and neither does. RS-08 and RS-25 mention LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory only as the target of forwarded supplier links — MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.4 and M.5a into LD.3 in RS-08, and StableReduction and ModularCurves stages into LD.3 and LD.6 in RS-25, each with a reason recording it as a section 15 forwarding of an inherited interface. Neither proposal has a `layers` entry for any stage of this roadmap, so none of its layers is narrowed, kept or dropped, and neither mentions FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration or ultraproducts.

findings.where: tauceti atlas stages LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.0, :LD.1 and :LD.2 — their prose Inputs against their `requires` fields, and the roadmap FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration
findings.claim: Three of the area's seven layers declare a prerequisite that is recorded nowhere and cannot be resolved. LD.0's Inputs are `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0`, LD.1's include `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4` and LD.2's include `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.2`. None of the three appears in that stage's `requires` field, and FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration is not in the atlas at all — not in the index, not among the roadmap extracts, and not in research/blueprint/roadmaps. The effect is worst at LD.0, the roadmap's base layer: its only declared input is unresolvable, and because `requires` is empty the atlas graph shows LD.0 as having no prerequisites, which is not what the layer says.
findings.evidence: LD.0's description reads '**Inputs.** `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0`' while its `requires` is the empty list; LD.1 reads '**Inputs.** `LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.0`, `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4`' with `requires` holding only LD.0; LD.2 reads '**Inputs.** `LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.1`, `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.2`' with `requires` holding only LD.1. The other four layers match: LD.3, LD.4, LD.5 and LD.6 have identical prose Inputs and `requires`, so the three mismatches are not the roadmap's convention. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration is absent from research/blueprint/atlas/index.json, has no file in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and none in research/blueprint/roadmaps/; every other stage id named by this roadmap resolves, and its own roadmap-level prerequisites (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion, DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles, SchemeAndStackFoundations) and its consumer AnalyticNumberTheory all exist. The roadmap is not fictional: content/campaign/FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration/README.md exists and carries sections LI.0 'Pinned libraries and declarations', LI.1, LI.2 'Analysis and topology', LI.3, LI.4 'Imported arithmetic foundations' and LI.5. The gap is wider than this area — 23 atlas roadmaps cite FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration stages 41 times in their stage prose, LI.0 through LI.4 — so the repair below is an area-level statement of a programme-level problem.
findings.fix: Two steps, the first inside this area and the second not. Within the area: add the named inputs to the `requires` of LD.0, LD.1 and LD.2 once they can be resolved, so that the recorded graph matches what the layers say. That depends on the second step, which belongs to whoever owns the atlas build: FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration has a document with stages LI.0 to LI.5 but no atlas record, so it should either be given one — an extract with its stages, like every other campaign roadmap — or, if it is deliberately outside the atlas as a library-integration note rather than a planned roadmap, the 41 citations of its stages across 23 roadmaps should be rewritten to name whatever does own that content. Until one or the other is done, no layer in the atlas can record a prerequisite on it, and this area's three layers misdescribe their own inputs.

findings.where: tauceti atlas stage LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.0, the clause on ultraproducts
findings.claim: LD.0 instructs a worker to construct mathematics the pinned library already has. Its text says 'Construct ultraproducts and prove the needed Los transfer theorem'. At Mathlib 082e2d3 both exist: Mathlib/ModelTheory/Ultraproducts.lean builds the ultraproduct structure and proves Los's theorem. A blueprint worker following LD.0 as written would rebuild them.
findings.evidence: LD.0: 'Define first-order ring/valued-field languages, structures, formulas, definable sets and interpretation in arithmetic fields; integrate model-theory foundations from Mathlib where available. Construct ultraproducts and prove the needed Los transfer theorem'. At the pin, Mathlib/ModelTheory/Ultraproducts.lean is headed '# Ultraproducts and Los's Theorem' and declares FirstOrder.Language.Ultraproduct.setoidPrestructure (line 49), the ultraproduct structure itself (line 74), funMap_cast (77), term_realize_cast (82), boundedFormula_realize_cast (95), realize_formula_cast (146) and sentence_realize (154), the last carrying the docstring '**Los's Theorem**: A sentence is true in an ultraproduct if and only if the set of structures it is true in is in the ultrafilter' and the statement '(u : Filter alpha).Product M |= phi <-> forall-eventually a in u, M a |= phi'. The file's own Main Results section names 'Los's Theorem: FirstOrder.Language.Ultraproduct.sentence_realize'. The surrounding first-order model theory is there too: 1238 declarations under FirstOrder.Language at the pin. This is the only clause of the layer that is out of date; the rest of LD.0, and the other layers' harder targets, are genuinely absent — searching the pin finds nothing for o-minimality or cell decomposition, Ax-Kochen-Ershov or Denef-Pas, motivic integration, Pila-Wilkie, Andre-Oort or Zilber-Pink, MRDP or Hilbert's tenth problem, or angular components.
findings.fix: Rewrite the clause so it imports rather than constructs: 'Import Mathlib's ultraproduct construction and Los's theorem (FirstOrder.Language.Ultraproduct.«structure» and FirstOrder.Language.Ultraproduct.sentence_realize), and add only the transfer interface this roadmap needs on top of them.' What LD.0 should still own is what Mathlib does not supply and the layer goes on to name: the valued-field languages, the interpretation of arithmetic fields, and the explicit elementary-extension and standard-part interface for nonstandard arithmetic. Record the same in AUDIT coverage for this layer when it is audited, so that the ultraproduct target is marked built rather than planned.
